q: The suspension of a railway servant under the Railway Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules is:

options.A: Not a penalty; it is an interim measure taken pending, or in contemplation of, disciplinary proceedings
options.B: A minor penalty
options.C: A major penalty
options.D: A penalty equivalent to withholding of increments

e: Suspension is not listed among the penalties; it is only an interim measure by which a servant is kept away from duty while disciplinary proceedings are pending or contemplated against him.

q: 'Censure' imposed on a railway servant under the Railway Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules is classified as:

options.A: A major penalty
options.B: A minor penalty
options.C: Not a penalty at all
options.D: An administrative warning having no penal effect

e: Censure, the mildest penalty expressing disapproval of the servant's conduct, is placed in the list of minor penalties under the Discipline and Appeal Rules.

q: 'Compulsory retirement' imposed on a railway servant as a measure of punishment under the Railway Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules is classified as:

options.A: A minor penalty
options.B: Not a penalty, being a retirement benefit
options.C: A major penalty
options.D: A penalty awardable only by the Railway Board

e: Compulsory retirement imposed as a punishment, distinct from retirement on superannuation, is classified as a major penalty because it cuts short the servant's career as a measure of penalty.

q: Withholding of passes and/or Privilege Ticket Orders admissible to a railway servant, imposed as a measure of punishment, is classified under the Railway Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules as:

options.A: A major penalty
options.B: Not a penalty under the Rules
options.C: A penalty awardable only on retirement
options.D: A minor penalty

e: Withholding of passes and/or Privilege Ticket Orders, a penalty peculiar to the Railways, is classified as a minor penalty under the Discipline and Appeal Rules.

q: In a departmental inquiry held under the Railway Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, the charged railway servant may take the assistance of:

options.A: Any other railway servant, including a retired railway servant, to present his case on his behalf
options.B: A legal practitioner in all cases, as of right
options.C: Only a member of his own family
options.D: No other person under any circumstances

e: The charged servant may take the assistance of another railway servant, including a retired railway servant, as defence assistant; engagement of a legal practitioner is not a matter of right.

q: The standard of proof required for establishing a charge in a departmental inquiry against a railway servant is:

options.A: Proof beyond reasonable doubt, as in a criminal trial
options.B: Preponderance of probability, i.e., the balance of probabilities
options.C: Mere suspicion based on the report of the vigilance organisation
options.D: Proof based solely on documentary evidence, oral evidence being inadmissible

e: A departmental inquiry is not a criminal trial, so charges are judged on preponderance of probability, i.e., the balance of probabilities, and not on proof beyond reasonable doubt.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Departmental proceedings may be instituted and continued against a railway servant even while criminal proceedings on the same facts are pending against him.
2. The acquittal of a railway servant in the criminal proceedings does not, by itself, bar the holding of departmental proceedings against him on the same facts.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: departmental and criminal proceedings are independent of each other, and an acquittal in court, which applies a stricter standard of proof, does not by itself bar departmental action on the same facts.

q: Where the period of suspension of a railway servant is prolonged for reasons directly attributable to the railway servant himself, the subsistence allowance payable to him for the period beyond three months may be:

options.A: Increased by an amount not exceeding 50% of the subsistence allowance admissible during the first three months
options.B: Withheld altogether
options.C: Converted into full pay and allowances
options.D: Decreased by an amount not exceeding 50% of the subsistence allowance admissible during the first three months

e: Where the servant himself is responsible for prolonging the suspension, the competent authority may reduce the subsistence allowance for the period beyond three months by up to 50 per cent.

q: The memorandum of charges issued to a railway servant for the imposition of a major penalty (Standard Form 5) is accompanied by:

options.A: A statement of the imputations of misconduct or misbehaviour, a list of documents and a list of witnesses by whom the articles of charge are proposed to be sustained
options.B: The final order of penalty proposed to be imposed
options.C: A copy of the report of the Comptroller and Auditor General
options.D: The personal file and service record of the railway servant

e: The major-penalty charge memorandum in Standard Form 5 is served with a statement of imputations of misconduct, a list of documents and a list of witnesses relied upon to sustain the charges.

q: A subscriber who exits from the National Pension System on attaining the age of 60 years may withdraw, as a lump sum, up to:

options.A: 40% of the accumulated pension wealth
options.B: 60% of the accumulated pension wealth
options.C: The entire accumulated pension wealth in all cases
options.D: 25% of the accumulated pension wealth

e: On exit from NPS at age 60, the subscriber may withdraw up to 60 per cent of the accumulated pension wealth as lump sum; at least 40 per cent must be used to purchase an annuity.

q: Under the Unified Pension Scheme, the assured payout admissible to a retired railway servant is protected against inflation by:

options.A: Revising the pay matrix every five years
options.B: Granting an ad hoc increase of 3% every year
options.C: Granting Dearness Relief on the assured payout, based on the All India Consumer Price Index for Industrial Workers
options.D: Linking the payout to the rate of Productivity Linked Bonus

e: Under the Unified Pension Scheme, the assured payout is protected against inflation through Dearness Relief granted on it on the basis of the All India Consumer Price Index for Industrial Workers.

q: Family pension is admissible to the family of a railway servant who dies while in service, provided he had rendered, at the time of his death, not less than:

options.A: Ten years of qualifying service
options.B: Five years of qualifying service
options.C: Twenty years of qualifying service
options.D: One year of service

e: Family pension on death in service is admissible even after a short service; the minimum service required for the family to become eligible is one year.

q: On fixation of pay in the pay matrix under the 7th CPC, where the pay computed after applying the fitment factor does not correspond exactly to any cell in the applicable Level, the pay is fixed at:

options.A: The next higher cell in that Level
options.B: The next lower cell in that Level
options.C: The minimum of that Level
options.D: The average of the two nearest cells

e: Where the pay computed with the fitment factor does not exactly match a cell in the Level, the pay is fixed at the next higher cell of that Level in the pay matrix.

q: Where the stages of pay of a railway servant are 'bunched' together on fixation of pay in the pay matrix, the benefit admissible to him is:

options.A: One additional increment for every two stages bunched
options.B: One additional increment for every three stages bunched
options.C: Two additional increments irrespective of the number of stages bunched
options.D: No benefit, bunching being ignored altogether

e: Where several pre-revision stages bunch together at the same cell, a bunching benefit in the form of an additional increment is admissible so that seniors are not placed at the same pay as juniors.

q: 'Substantive pay' of a railway servant means:

options.A: The pay drawn by him in an officiating appointment
options.B: The personal pay granted to him on personal considerations
options.C: The pay, other than special pay, personal pay or emoluments classed as pay, to which he is entitled on account of a post to which he has been appointed substantively
options.D: The pay fixed provisionally pending issue of regular fixation orders

e: Substantive pay is the pay, other than special pay, personal pay or emoluments classed as pay, attached to a post to which the servant has been appointed substantively, i.e., on a permanent basis.

q: When a railway servant is appointed to officiate in a higher post, he is entitled to:

options.A: Only the pay of his substantive post, without any benefit
options.B: The pay of the higher post plus his substantive pay
options.C: A fixed officiating allowance of 10% of his substantive pay
options.D: The pay of the higher post, fixed under the rules governing pay fixation on promotion

e: On officiating appointment to a higher post, the servant draws the pay of the higher post, fixed in accordance with the rules governing pay fixation on promotion.

q: A railway servant who retires from service on 30th June, and whose annual increment falls due on the 1st July following, is entitled, for the purpose of pensionary benefits, to:

options.A: One notional increment, as if it had been drawn on the date of retirement
options.B: No increment, as he was not in service on the due date
options.C: Two notional increments by way of compensation
options.D: A notional increment only if he had completed 35 years of service

e: A servant retiring a day before his increment date, such as retirement on 30th June with increment due on 1st July, gets one notional increment for computing pensionary benefits.

q: A railway servant who undergoes sterilisation operation after having two surviving children is granted, as an incentive for promoting the small family norm:

options.A: One advance increment which is merged in his pay for all purposes
options.B: A special increment in the form of personal pay, equal in amount to the rate of increment due at the time of sterilisation, which is not absorbed in future increments
options.C: A lump sum cash award equal to three months' pay
options.D: Two additional days of casual leave every year

e: The sterilisation incentive is a special increment in the form of personal pay, equal to the increment rate at the time of the operation, which is not absorbed in future increments.

q: Dearness Allowance admissible to a railway servant is calculated as a percentage of his:

options.A: Gross emoluments including all allowances
options.B: Basic pay plus House Rent Allowance
options.C: Basic pay
options.D: Basic pay plus Transport Allowance

e: Dearness Allowance is calculated as a percentage of the basic pay of the servant in the pay matrix, and not on allowances such as HRA or Transport Allowance.

q: The leave salary admissible to a female railway servant during a period of maternity leave is equal to:

options.A: Half of the pay drawn immediately before proceeding on leave
options.B: The pay drawn immediately before proceeding on leave, without Dearness Allowance
options.C: A fixed amount equal to the minimum pay of her Level
options.D: The salary (pay and allowances) last drawn by her before proceeding on leave

e: During maternity leave, the female servant is entitled to leave salary equal to the full salary, that is the pay and allowances last drawn by her before proceeding on leave.

q: Maternity leave admissible to a female railway servant in case of miscarriage, including abortion, is:

options.A: 45 days during her entire service
options.B: 90 days during her entire service
options.C: 30 days on each occasion, without any limit
options.D: Not admissible in such cases

e: For miscarriage including abortion, maternity leave is admissible for a total period of 45 days during the entire service of the female railway servant.

q: Paternity leave admissible to a male railway servant may be availed of during the period:

options.A: Only after the delivery of the child is over
options.B: Commencing 15 days before, or up to six months after, the date of delivery of the child
options.C: Only within 15 days after the date of delivery
options.D: At any time before the child attains the age of five years

e: Paternity leave of 15 days may be availed of during the confinement window beginning 15 days before the delivery and extending up to six months after the date of delivery.

q: Child Care Leave is admissible to a railway servant for taking care of a disabled child up to the age of:

options.A: 18 years
options.B: 25 years
options.C: 22 years
options.D: There is no age limit in the case of a disabled child

e: Child Care Leave covers a child up to 18 years of age generally, but in the case of a disabled child the age limit is extended up to 22 years. The keyed answer is C.

q: Child Care Leave cannot be granted to a railway servant in a spell of less than:

options.A: 5 days
options.B: 30 days
options.C: 10 days
options.D: 15 days

e: Child Care Leave cannot be granted in spells of less than 15 days at a time, so that it is availed in reasonably long spells for the care of the child.

q: Child Adoption Leave admissible to a female railway servant, with less than two surviving children, who adopts a child below the age of one year, is:

options.A: 180 days
options.B: 90 days
options.C: 135 days
options.D: 60 days

e: A female servant with less than two surviving children who legally adopts a child below one year of age is entitled to Child Adoption Leave of 180 days.

q: Commuted leave granted to a railway servant on medical certificate during his entire service shall not exceed:

options.A: One-fourth of the Leave on Half Average Pay at his credit
options.B: Half the amount of Leave on Half Average Pay due to him
options.C: The full amount of Leave on Half Average Pay at his credit
options.D: 90 days in all

e: Commuted leave, granted on medical certificate by debiting Leave on Half Average Pay at double rate, cannot exceed half the amount of Leave on Half Average Pay due to the servant.

q: The period of joining time availed of by a railway servant on transfer in public interest is treated as:

options.A: Leave on Average Pay debited to his leave account
options.B: Extra Ordinary Leave
options.C: Duty for all purposes, during which he draws pay equal to the pay drawn before relinquishing charge of the old post
options.D: Dies non, not counting for any service benefit

e: Joining time on transfer in public interest is treated as duty for all purposes, and the servant draws during it the pay equal to that drawn before relinquishing charge of the old post.

q: A railway servant who has availed leave on medical certificate shall not return to duty unless he first produces:

options.A: A certificate from his controlling officer permitting him to resume duty
options.B: A fresh medical examination report from the Railway Board
options.C: An undertaking that he will not avail leave again for one year
options.D: A medical certificate of fitness from the competent medical authority

e: A servant who has availed leave on medical certificate cannot resume duty unless he first produces a medical certificate of fitness from the competent medical authority.

q: Hostel subsidy, admissible to a railway servant under the Children Education Allowance scheme where a child is studying in a hostel away from the station of posting, is reimbursed at the rate of:

options.A: Rs 8437.50 per month per child
options.B: Rs 2,250 per month per child
options.C: Rs 1,000 per month per child
options.D: Rs 10,000 per month per child

e: Hostel Subsidy is now Rs 8,437.50 per month per child, so a statement quoting the old Rs 6,750 ceiling is no longer correct. (Source: DoPT OM No. A-27012/01/2023-Pers.Policy(Allowance) dated 25.04.2024; effective 01.01.2024.)

q: House Rent Allowance is NOT admissible to a railway servant:

options.A: Who resides in a house owned by his father
options.B: Whose spouse has been allotted Government accommodation at the same station
options.C: Who resides in a rented house in a 'Z' class city
options.D: Who is posted at a station where no railway quarter is available

e: HRA is not admissible where the spouse of the servant has been allotted Government accommodation at the same station, since the family is deemed to be provided with accommodation.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A railway servant transferred in public interest may be permitted to retain the railway quarter at the old station for a period of two months on payment of normal licence fee.
2. Retention of the quarter beyond the initial two months may be permitted for a further period of two months on payment of double the licence fee.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: on transfer in public interest the quarter at the old station may be retained for two months on normal licence fee, and for a further two months on double the licence fee.

q: A Group 'C' railway servant who has completed less than five years of service is entitled to privilege passes in a calendar year up to:

options.A: Three sets
options.B: Six sets
options.C: Two sets
options.D: One set

e: Privilege passes are scaled to length of service; a Group C servant with less than five years of service is entitled to only one set of privilege passes in a calendar year.

q: On the death of a retired railway servant, complimentary passes admissible to his widow are issued at the rate of:

options.A: Half the number of sets of passes that were admissible to the deceased railway servant
options.B: The same number of sets as were admissible to the deceased railway servant
options.C: One-fourth of the number admissible to the deceased railway servant
options.D: No passes are admissible to the widow

e: On the death of a retired railway servant, complimentary passes are issued to his widow at the rate of half the number of sets that were admissible to the deceased servant.

q: Where a railway servant has a family, a nomination made by him for Death-cum-Retirement Gratuity can be made:

options.A: In favour of any person, whether a member of his family or not
options.B: Only in favour of a member or members of his family
options.C: Only in favour of his spouse
options.D: Only in favour of a Government institution

e: Where the servant has a family, the nomination for Death-cum-Retirement Gratuity can be made only in favour of a member or members of his family, and not in favour of an outsider.

q: The additional quantum of pension admissible to a railway pensioner on attaining the age of 100 years is:

options.A: 50% of the basic pension
options.B: 60% of the basic pension
options.C: 100% of the basic pension
options.D: 80% of the basic pension

e: The additional quantum of pension rises with age, and on attaining 100 years the pensioner gets an additional pension equal to 100 per cent of the basic pension.

q: Under the extant instructions on confirmation of Government servants, a railway servant is required to be confirmed:

options.A: On every promotion to a higher post
options.B: Once every five years of service
options.C: Separately in every grade to which he is promoted
options.D: Only once, in the entry grade/post of the service to which he is appointed

e: Under the extant instructions, a Government servant is confirmed only once, in the entry grade or post of the service to which he is recruited, and not again on every promotion.

q: The adverse entries recorded in the Annual Performance Appraisal Report (Annual Confidential Report) of a railway servant are required to be:

options.A: Communicated to the railway servant concerned
options.B: Kept secret from the railway servant in all cases
options.C: Communicated only at the time of his retirement
options.D: Communicated only if he is to be considered for promotion

e: Adverse entries in the Annual Performance Appraisal Report must be communicated to the servant concerned so that he can represent against them and improve his performance.

q: The inter-se seniority of direct recruits and promotees appointed to a grade on the Railways is determined by:

options.A: Their respective ages
options.B: Rotation of vacancies in accordance with the quota prescribed for direct recruitment and promotion to that grade
options.C: The date of issue of the panel in all cases
options.D: The marks obtained in the departmental examination alone

e: The inter-se seniority of direct recruits and promotees in a grade is fixed by rotation of vacancies according to the prescribed quota for direct recruitment and promotion.

q: Under the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966, a railway servant shall not:

options.A: Open a savings bank account in the name of his spouse
options.B: Accept any salary for the period of his authorised leave
options.C: Lend money to, or borrow money from, a person with whom he has official dealings, or otherwise engage in money-lending
options.D: Purchase consumer goods on instalments from a cooperative store

e: The Conduct Rules prohibit a railway servant from resorting to, or in any way abetting, any form of strike or coercion in connection with service matters.

q: A second appeal against the orders of the First Appellate Authority under the Right to Information Act, 2005 lies to the Central Information Commission and must be filed within:

options.A: 30 days from the date of the order
options.B: 45 days from the date of the order
options.C: 60 days from the date of the order
options.D: 90 days from the date of the order

e: A second appeal against the order of the First Appellate Authority under the RTI Act lies to the Central Information Commission and must be filed within 90 days of the order.

q: In the matter of hours of work and periods of rest, staff employed in railway workshops are governed by:

options.A: The Factories Act, 1948, railway workshops being factories within the meaning of that Act
options.B: The Hours of Employment Regulations alone
options.C: The Industrial Disputes Act, 1947
options.D: No statutory provision, the matter being regulated departmentally

e: Railway workshops are factories within the meaning of the Factories Act, 1948, so hours of work and rest of workshop staff are governed by that Act and not by the Hours of Employment Regulations.

q: The case of a Group 'C' railway servant for premature retirement in public interest is ordinarily reviewed on his attaining the age of 55 years or on completion of:

options.A: 20 years of qualifying service, whichever is earlier
options.B: 30 years of qualifying service, whichever is earlier
options.C: 25 years of qualifying service, whichever is later
options.D: 33 years of qualifying service, whichever is later

e: The case of a Group C servant for premature retirement in public interest is ordinarily reviewed on attaining 55 years of age or on completion of 30 years of qualifying service, whichever is earlier.

q: A railway servant who is medically decategorised and cannot immediately be absorbed in a suitable alternative post is:

options.A: Retired from service forthwith on invalid pension
options.B: Treated as being on Extra Ordinary Leave without pay
options.C: Borne on a supernumerary post in his grade until he is absorbed in a suitable alternative post
options.D: Reverted to the lowest post in his cadre

e: A medically decategorised servant who cannot immediately be absorbed is borne on a supernumerary post in his own grade, protecting his pay, until a suitable alternative post is found.

q: On the retirement of a member of the Central Government Employees Group Insurance Scheme, the amount payable to him is:

options.A: Only the amount subscribed by him, without interest
options.B: The insurance cover amount of his group
options.C: A fixed sum of Rs 30,000 in all cases
options.D: The amount at his credit in the Savings Fund of the Scheme, together with interest thereon

e: On retirement, a member of CGEGIS receives the amount accumulated at his credit in the Savings Fund of the Scheme together with interest, as only part of the subscription went to the Insurance Fund.

q: A railway servant retires on superannuation with 300 days of Leave on Average Pay at his credit. His basic pay at retirement is Rs 70,000 per month and the rate of Dearness Allowance admissible is 50%. The cash equivalent of leave salary payable to him is:
e: Cash equivalent = (pay + DA) x days/30 = (70,000 + 35,000) x 300/30 = Rs 1,05,000 x 10 = Rs 10,50,000, for the maximum 300 days of Leave on Average Pay.

q: Where a railway servant is transferred in public interest to a post carrying a lower rate of pay, the difference between the pay drawn by him in the old post and the pay admissible in the new post is:

options.A: Forfeited permanently by him
options.B: Granted to him as personal pay, to be absorbed in his future increments
options.C: Paid to him as a one-time lump sum compensation
options.D: Allowed only if he had completed 20 years of service in the old post

e: On transfer in public interest to a lower-paid post, the shortfall is protected as personal pay, which is absorbed in the increments the servant earns thereafter.

q: The period of deputation of a railway servant to an ex-cadre post shall ordinarily not exceed:

options.A: One year, without any provision for extension
options.B: Two years, extendable up to three years
options.C: Five years, extendable up to seven years as a routine
options.D: Three years, which may be extended in exceptional cases by up to two more years

e: Deputation to an ex-cadre post is ordinarily limited to three years, and may be extended in exceptional cases by up to two more years, making five years the normal maximum.

q: The inter-se seniority of railway servants who are promoted on the basis of a selection is determined by:

options.A: Their order of position (merit) in the selection panel
options.B: The dates on which they actually assume charge of the higher post
options.C: Their dates of birth
options.D: The dates of their initial appointment in the Railways

e: For promotions made through selection, the inter-se seniority of the selected servants is determined by their order of merit in the selection panel.

q: A railway servant who, on being selected for promotion, refuses to accept the promotion is debarred from being considered for promotion for a period of:

options.A: Six months
options.B: Two years
options.C: One year
options.D: Three years

e: A servant who refuses an offered promotion forfeits his turn and is debarred from consideration for promotion for a period of one year.

q: A railway servant attains the age of superannuation (60 years) on 15th March, 2027. He will retire from service on:

options.A: The afternoon of 15th March, 2027
options.B: The afternoon of 31st March, 2027
options.C: The afternoon of 14th March, 2027
options.D: The afternoon of 30th April, 2027

e: A railway servant retires on the afternoon of the last day of the month in which he attains the age of superannuation, so attaining 60 on 15th March 2027 means retirement on 31st March 2027.

q: The drawal of annual increments of railway servants in a pay bill is supported by:

options.A: An Increment Certificate signed by the competent authority, accompanying the pay bill
options.B: A Last Pay Certificate issued by the previous office
options.C: A copy of the leave account of each railway servant
options.D: A certificate of the Accounts Office verifying the service books

e: Annual increments in a pay bill are drawn on the strength of an Increment Certificate signed by the competent authority, which accompanies the pay bill to the Accounts Office.

q: The entries made in the Service Book of a railway servant are required to be verified and attested by the Head of Office:

options.A: Once in five years
options.B: Only at the time of his retirement
options.C: Once in three years
options.D: Every year

e: Every entry in the Service Book must be attested by the Head of Office, and the entries are required to be verified and attested every year.

q: In regard to qualifying service for pension, the period spent by a person as an apprentice on the Railways:

options.A: Counts in full as qualifying service
options.B: Counts to the extent of one-half
options.C: Does not count as qualifying service, as an apprentice is not a railway servant
options.D: Counts only if the apprenticeship exceeds two years

e: An apprentice is not a railway servant, since he is engaged only for training, so the period of apprenticeship does not count as qualifying service for pension.

q: A person shall not be appointed substantively to a post on the Railways unless:

options.A: He has been medically examined and has furnished a certificate of health as required under the rules
options.B: He has completed two years of temporary service
options.C: He has attained the age of 25 years
options.D: He has passed a departmental examination

e: A person cannot be appointed substantively to a post unless he has been medically examined and has furnished the prescribed certificate of health and fitness.

q: Temporary service rendered by a railway servant in a post, followed without interruption by his confirmation in the same or another post:

options.A: Does not count as qualifying service for pension
options.B: Counts as qualifying service for pension
options.C: Counts only to the extent of one-half for pension
options.D: Counts only if the temporary service exceeded ten years

e: Temporary service in a post followed, without interruption, by confirmation in the same or another post counts in full as qualifying service for pension.

q: A railway servant who has tendered his resignation may withdraw it:

options.A: At any time, even after it has taken effect
options.B: Only within seven days of tendering it
options.C: Not at all, once it is tendered
options.D: Before the resignation becomes effective, with the permission of the appointing authority

e: A resignation may be withdrawn before it becomes effective, but only with the permission of the appointing authority; once effective, it cannot be withdrawn.

q: House Rent Allowance continues to be admissible to a railway servant during a period of leave, provided the prescribed conditions are fulfilled, for a period not exceeding:

options.A: 90 days
options.B: 120 days
options.C: 180 days
options.D: 365 days

e: HRA remains admissible during leave, subject to the prescribed conditions such as continued occupation of the house, for a period not exceeding 180 days.

q: Quarantine leave is granted to a railway servant when:

options.A: His attendance at office is prevented by reason of an infectious disease in his family, on the certificate of the competent public health authority
options.B: He proceeds on a pilgrimage
options.C: He is admitted to a hospital for a surgical operation
options.D: He is ordered by his controlling officer to remain away from office for indiscipline

e: Quarantine leave is granted when the servant's attendance is prevented by an infectious disease in his family, on the certificate of the competent public health authority.

q: A railway servant who overstays his leave, i.e., remains absent after the expiry of the leave sanctioned to him, is:

options.A: Entitled to leave salary for the period of overstayal in all cases
options.B: Treated as on duty for the period of overstayal
options.C: Granted leave for the period of overstayal automatically by the Accounts Office
options.D: Not entitled to any leave salary for the period of absence in excess of the leave, and such period may be treated as Extra Ordinary Leave

e: For the period of overstayal of leave the servant is not entitled to any leave salary, and the excess absence may be regularised by treating it as Extra Ordinary Leave.

q: A railway servant who is recalled to duty compulsorily, before the expiry of the leave sanctioned to him, is entitled to:

options.A: Payment of double salary for the unexpired portion of the leave
options.B: Travelling allowance for the journey undertaken by him to join duty on recall
options.C: A fresh spell of leave equal to twice the unexpired portion of the leave
options.D: No facility of any kind

e: A servant compulsorily recalled to duty before the expiry of his sanctioned leave is entitled to travelling allowance for the journey undertaken to rejoin duty on recall.

q: Leave granted to a railway servant as leave preparatory to retirement:

options.A: May extend up to six months beyond the date of retirement
options.B: Is admissible only in the form of Leave on Half Average Pay
options.C: Cannot extend beyond the date on which he is due to retire from service
options.D: Is debited to the leave account of the succeeding year

e: Leave preparatory to retirement can be availed only up to the date of retirement and cannot extend beyond the date on which the servant is due to retire.

q: A railway servant to whom study leave is granted for pursuing a course of study is required to:

options.A: Execute a bond undertaking to serve the Railways for the specified period after his return from the study leave
options.B: Deposit the entire leave salary drawn by him as security with the Railways
options.C: Resign from service before proceeding on the leave
options.D: Surrender his lien on the post held by him

e: Study leave is granted subject to the servant executing a bond undertaking to serve the Railways for the specified period after returning from the study leave.

q: Under the Factories Act, 1948, applicable to staff employed in railway workshops, an adult worker who has worked for a period of 240 days or more in a calendar year is entitled in the subsequent year to leave with wages at the rate of:

options.A: One day for every 10 days of work performed by him
options.B: One day for every 15 days of work performed by him
options.C: One day for every 25 days of work performed by him
options.D: One day for every 20 days of work performed by him

e: Under the Factories Act, an adult worker who has worked 240 days or more in a calendar year earns leave with wages at one day for every 20 days of work in the subsequent year.

q: The leave account of a gazetted railway servant is maintained by:

options.A: The office in which he is himself working
options.B: The Accounts Office
options.C: The Railway Board
options.D: The Personnel Branch of the Zonal Railway Headquarters

e: The leave account of a gazetted railway servant is maintained by the Accounts Office, whereas that of a non-gazetted servant is maintained in his own office.

q: For computing the cash equivalent of leave salary payable to a railway servant on retirement against the Leave on Average Pay at his credit, which of the following is NOT reckoned?

options.A: The pay drawn by him on the date of retirement
options.B: Dearness Allowance admissible on such pay
options.C: House Rent Allowance
options.D: None of the above, as all allowances drawn are reckoned

e: In computing the cash equivalent of leave salary, only pay and the Dearness Allowance admissible on it are reckoned; House Rent Allowance is not taken into account.

q: Where departmental or judicial proceedings are pending against a railway servant at the time of his retirement, the provisional pension sanctioned to him is equal to:

options.A: The maximum pension which would have been admissible to him on the basis of the qualifying service rendered up to the date of retirement
options.B: 50% of the pension which would have been admissible to him
options.C: 75% of the pension which would have been admissible to him
options.D: The minimum pension prescribed under the rules

e: Where proceedings are pending at retirement, provisional pension is sanctioned at the maximum amount that would be admissible on the qualifying service rendered up to the date of retirement.

q: Where a deceased railway servant leaves behind two widows, the family pension admissible is:

options.A: Paid only to the elder widow
options.B: Paid only to the widow who was living with him at the time of his death
options.C: Paid to his children, and not to the widows
options.D: Divided equally between the two widows

e: Where a deceased servant leaves two widows who are both eligible, the family pension is divided equally between the two widows.

q: The National Pension System is applicable to railway servants who joined railway service:

options.A: On or after 1st January, 2016
options.B: On or after 1st January, 2004
options.C: On or after 1st April, 2006
options.D: On or after 1st January, 2000

e: The National Pension System replaced the old pension scheme for railway servants who joined service on or after 1st January 2004.

q: Under the National Pension System, registration of subscribers, allotment of the Permanent Retirement Account Number (PRAN) and maintenance of subscribers' accounts are the functions of the:

options.A: Pension Fund Managers
options.B: Points of Presence
options.C: Central Recordkeeping Agency (CRA)
options.D: Annuity Service Providers

e: Under NPS, the Central Recordkeeping Agency maintains subscribers' accounts, allots the Permanent Retirement Account Number (PRAN) and registers subscribers; Pension Fund Managers only invest the funds.

q: Under the Unified Pension Scheme, where a subscriber dies after his retirement, the family payout admissible to his legally wedded spouse is:

options.A: 50% of the payout admissible to the subscriber
options.B: 30% of the payout admissible to the subscriber
options.C: 100% of the payout admissible to the subscriber
options.D: 60% of the payout admissible to the subscriber immediately before his death

e: Under the Unified Pension Scheme, on the death of the retired subscriber, the legally wedded spouse gets a family payout of 60 per cent of the payout admissible to the subscriber immediately before his death.

q: Under the Unified Pension Scheme, the contribution payable by the railway servant (employee) to his individual corpus is:

options.A: 10% of Basic Pay plus Dearness Allowance
options.B: 14% of Basic Pay plus Dearness Allowance
options.C: 18.5% of Basic Pay plus Dearness Allowance
options.D: 8.33% of Basic Pay plus Dearness Allowance

e: Under the Unified Pension Scheme, the employee contributes 10 per cent of Basic Pay plus Dearness Allowance to his individual corpus, with a matching contribution structure from the Government.

q: The amount of pension and family pension admissible to a railway pensioner is rounded off:

options.A: To the nearest ten rupees
options.B: To the next lower rupee
options.C: To the next higher rupee
options.D: It is paid in exact paise, without any rounding off

e: Pension and family pension are rounded off to the next higher rupee, so that the pensioner is never paid a fraction less than the amount worked out.

q: A railway pensioner's monthly pension is Rs 45,000. He commutes 40% of his pension. Taking the commutation factor for his age on the next birthday (60 years) as 8.371, the lump sum commuted value payable to him is:
e: Commuted value = monthly commuted portion x factor x 12 = (45,000 x 40 per cent) x 8.371 x 12 = 18,000 x 8.371 x 12 = Rs 18,08,136.

q: A railway servant retires on superannuation with 240 days of Leave on Average Pay at his credit. His basic pay at retirement is Rs 56,000 per month and Dearness Allowance is admissible at 50%. The cash equivalent of leave salary payable to him is:
e: Cash equivalent = (pay + DA) x days/30 = (56,000 + 28,000) x 240/30 = Rs 84,000 x 8 = Rs 6,72,000, for 240 days of Leave on Average Pay.

q: The pension of a railway pensioner is admissible:

options.A: For and up to and including the day of his death
options.B: Only up to the last day of the month preceding his death
options.C: Up to the date on which the life certificate was last furnished by him
options.D: For a maximum period of 30 years from the date of retirement

e: Pension is admissible for the day of the pensioner's death as well; it ceases only from the following day, so it is payable up to and including the day of death.

q: 'Reduction to a lower stage in the same time scale of pay for a specified period, with further directions as to whether the railway servant will or will not earn increments during the period of reduction' is classified under the Railway Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules as:

options.A: A minor penalty
options.B: Not a penalty at all
options.C: A major penalty
options.D: An administrative measure

e: Reduction to a lower stage in the same time scale, with directions about earning increments during the reduction, seriously affects pay and is therefore classified as a major penalty.

q: Where the disciplinary authority disagrees with the findings of the Inquiring Authority on any article of charge, it shall, before passing final orders:

options.A: Order a fresh inquiry by another Inquiring Authority in every case
options.B: Record its reasons for such disagreement together with its own findings, communicate the same to the charged railway servant and give him an opportunity to make a representation
options.C: Impose the penalty without communicating anything to the charged railway servant
options.D: Refer the case to the Railway Board for orders

e: Before differing from the Inquiring Authority, the disciplinary authority must record its reasons and its own findings, communicate them to the charged servant and consider his representation before passing final orders.

q: An order placing a railway servant under suspension may be made by:

options.A: Any officer who is senior to the railway servant
options.B: Only the General Manager of the Railway
options.C: Only the Railway Board
options.D: The appointing authority, or any authority to which the appointing authority is subordinate, or any other authority empowered in that behalf

e: An order of suspension may be made by the appointing authority, by any authority to which it is subordinate, or by any other authority empowered in that behalf by the competent authority.

q: Where two or more railway servants are involved in the same disciplinary case, the competent authority may:

options.A: Order that the disciplinary action against all of them be taken in a common proceeding
options.B: Proceed only against the senior-most of them
options.C: Drop the proceedings, as joint proceedings are not permitted
options.D: Refer all of them directly to a criminal court

e: Where two or more railway servants are involved in the same case, the competent authority may direct that disciplinary action against all of them be taken in a common proceeding.

q: Departmental proceedings instituted against a railway servant while he was in service, but not concluded before his retirement:

options.A: Lapse automatically on his retirement
options.B: Are converted into criminal proceedings
options.C: Are deemed to have been continued after his retirement as proceedings under the pension rules, as if he had continued in service
options.D: Can be continued only with the permission of the Central Administrative Tribunal

e: Proceedings begun during service but not concluded before retirement are deemed to continue after retirement as proceedings under the pension rules, as if the servant had continued in service.

q: Under the Railway Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, no appeal lies against:

options.A: An order placing a railway servant under suspension
options.B: An order passed by the President of India
options.C: An order imposing a minor penalty
options.D: An order passed by the appellate authority enhancing the penalty

e: No appeal lies against an order passed by the President of India; orders of suspension and of penalty by other authorities are appealable under the Rules.

q: A Group 'A' railway officer who accepts a gift from a near relative or a personal friend having no official dealings with him, on an occasion such as a marriage or a religious function, is required to report the matter to the Government if the value of the gift exceeds:
e: A Group A officer must report to the Government a gift received from a near relative or personal friend having no official dealings with him when its value exceeds Rs 25,000.

q: A railway servant who proposes to enter into a transaction in respect of immovable property with a person having official dealings with him is required to:

options.A: Obtain the previous sanction of the prescribed authority for the transaction
options.B: Merely inform his controlling officer after the transaction is completed
options.C: Do nothing, as no intimation or sanction is required in such cases
options.D: Deposit the property documents with the Accounts Office

e: A transaction in immovable property with a person having official dealings with the servant requires the previous sanction of the prescribed authority under the Conduct Rules.

q: Under the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966, speculation in stocks, shares or other investments by a railway servant is prohibited. In this context, which of the following is treated as speculation?

options.A: An occasional investment made through a recognised stock broker
options.B: Investment in Government securities
options.C: Frequent purchase or sale of shares, securities or other investments
options.D: A one-time subscription to a public issue of shares

e: Speculation means frequent purchase or sale of shares, securities or investments; an occasional investment through a recognised broker is not treated as speculation.

q: Under the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966, a railway servant shall so manage his private affairs as to avoid:

options.A: Opening of a savings bank account
options.B: Purchase of consumer goods on instalments
options.C: Any borrowing whatsoever, including from a bank
options.D: Habitual indebtedness or insolvency, and he is required to report the fact if he is adjudged or declared insolvent

e: The Conduct Rules require a servant to manage his private affairs so as to avoid habitual indebtedness or insolvency, and to report the fact if he is adjudged or declared insolvent.

q: A person aggrieved by the decision of the Central Public Information Officer under the Right to Information Act, 2005 may prefer the first appeal to the First Appellate Authority within:

options.A: 15 days from the expiry of the period for furnishing the information or from the receipt of the decision
options.B: 30 days from the expiry of the period for furnishing the information or from the receipt of the decision
options.C: 60 days from the receipt of the decision
options.D: 90 days from the receipt of the decision

e: The first appeal under the RTI Act must be preferred within 30 days from the expiry of the period allowed for furnishing information or from the receipt of the CPIO's decision.

q: The maximum amount of penalty that can be imposed on a Central Public Information Officer under the Right to Information Act, 2005, at the rate of Rs 250 for each day of default, is:
e: The penalty on a CPIO under the RTI Act is imposed at Rs 250 for each day of default, but the total penalty cannot exceed Rs 25,000.

q: Under the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966, a railway servant shall not have recourse to any court or to the press for the vindication of any official act of his which has been the subject-matter of adverse criticism, unless:

options.A: He has completed 20 years of service
options.B: He has retired from service
options.C: He has obtained the previous sanction of the Government
options.D: The criticism was made by a subordinate officer

e: A railway servant cannot approach a court or the press to vindicate an official act that has been criticised, unless he has obtained the previous sanction of the Government.

q: Under the Hours of Employment Regulations, staff classified as 'Intensive' are entitled to a period of rest in a week of not less than:

options.A: 24 consecutive hours
options.B: 30 consecutive hours including one full night
options.C: 48 consecutive hours
options.D: 36 consecutive hours including one full night

e: Under the Hours of Employment Regulations, staff classified as Intensive, who work under sustained pressure, are entitled to weekly rest of not less than 36 consecutive hours including one full night.

q: The classification of an employment under the Hours of Employment Regulations into the categories 'Intensive', 'Continuous', 'Essentially Intermittent' or 'Excluded' is determined on the basis of:

options.A: The seniority of the staff employed
options.B: A job analysis of the work involved in the employment
options.C: The pay level of the post
options.D: The choice exercised by the staff themselves

e: The classification of employments as Intensive, Continuous, Essentially Intermittent or Excluded is decided on the basis of a job analysis of the work performed in the employment.

q: Leave of a railway servant is governed by the principle that:

options.A: Leave can be claimed as a matter of right by every railway servant
options.B: Leave cannot be claimed as a matter of right, and it may be refused or revoked by the sanctioning authority in the exigencies of public service
options.C: Leave once sanctioned can never be revoked by the authority
options.D: A railway servant is entitled to avail leave on the day he applies for it

e: Leave is not a matter of right; the sanctioning authority may refuse or revoke it in the exigencies of public service, even after it has been sanctioned.

q: The leave salary payable to a railway servant during a period of Leave Not Due is equal to:

options.A: The leave salary admissible during Leave on Average Pay
options.B: Nil, as Leave Not Due carries no leave salary
options.C: 75 per cent of the leave salary admissible during Leave on Average Pay
options.D: The leave salary admissible during Leave on Half Average Pay

e: Leave Not Due is granted in anticipation of Leave on Half Average Pay to be earned later, and carries leave salary equal to that admissible during Leave on Half Average Pay.

q: Commuted leave is ordinarily granted to a railway servant:

options.A: On the production of a medical certificate from the authorised medical officer
options.B: Without any medical certificate, on his own request
options.C: Only for prosecuting higher studies abroad
options.D: Only after the Leave on Average Pay at his credit is exhausted

e: Commuted leave is ordinarily granted only on production of a medical certificate from the authorised medical officer recommending rest for the servant.

q: A railway servant is transferred in public interest to a station involving a journey of about 800 kilometres. The joining time admissible to him is:

options.A: 10 days
options.B: 12 days
options.C: 15 days
options.D: 8 days

e: Joining time is graded by the distance involved in the transfer; for a journey of about 800 kilometres, the admissible joining time is 10 days.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Home Town Leave Travel Concession is admissible to a railway servant once in a block of two years.
2. All India Leave Travel Concession can be availed in a block of four years, in lieu of one Home Town Leave Travel Concession of that block.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: Home Town LTC is admissible once in a block of two years, and All India LTC may be availed in a four-year block in lieu of one Home Town LTC of that block.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Maternity leave granted to a female railway servant is not debited to her leave account.
2. Paternity leave granted to a male railway servant is debited to his Leave on Average Pay account.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is correct because maternity leave is not debited to the leave account. Statement 2 is wrong because paternity leave also is granted without any debit to the Leave on Average Pay account.

q: A railway servant who is transferred at his own request, and whose transfer is not treated as being in public interest, is entitled to:

options.A: Travelling Allowance and Composite Transfer Grant as admissible on a transfer in public interest
options.B: Travelling Allowance only, but not Composite Transfer Grant
options.C: Neither Travelling Allowance nor Composite Transfer Grant
options.D: Composite Transfer Grant only

e: A transfer at the servant's own request, not treated as in public interest, carries neither Travelling Allowance nor Composite Transfer Grant.

q: The pay of an officer directly recruited to a Group 'A' post in the Junior Time Scale on the Indian Railways is fixed in:

options.A: Level 9 of the pay matrix
options.B: Level 10 of the pay matrix
options.C: Level 11 of the pay matrix
options.D: Level 12 of the pay matrix

e: An officer directly recruited to a Group A post in the Junior Time Scale starts his service in Level 10 of the pay matrix.

q: Non-Practising Allowance drawn by a railway medical officer is treated as pay for the purposes of:

options.A: Dearness Allowance and retirement benefits
options.B: Income tax exemption only
options.C: No purpose at all
options.D: Travelling Allowance only

e: Non-Practising Allowance drawn by railway medical officers is treated as pay for the purposes of Dearness Allowance and for retirement benefits.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Children Education Allowance is admissible in respect of the two eldest surviving children of a railway servant.
2. Children Education Allowance is admissible for a child studying from nursery level up to Class XII.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: Children Education Allowance is payable for the two eldest surviving children, and it covers studies from nursery level up to Class XII.
